tasks.title: Gate-shape lint rule 3: reject a gate that inspects a HEAD file its task does not own
tasks.goal: Three of the five stalled production runs had a verify command that read a file the task was not assigned; the driver's gate_files_moved() reverts exactly that file before the gate runs, so no implementation could ever pass. This task makes the plan-time gate-shape lint in .loop/run.sh compute that same condition one phase earlier and refuse the plan, while leaving gates that merely execute such a file (a test runner, bash some-script) alone. It is the first of the plan-time refusals; T2 and T4 extend the same lint and the same SKILL section. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.
acceptance: A plan is rejected by the existing gate-shape lint in .loop/run.sh — die, exit 1, before any iteration — when a task's verify names, in an inspecting position, a path that exists in HEAD and is absent from that task's files array. Inspecting covers at least grep, cat, test -f and a language-level file read such as Python open(...).read().

The rejection line names the task id and then the offending path on the same line, in the existing '    <id>  <reason>' shape, and says why it is unpassable (the driver reverts that file before the gate runs).

Accepted, with nothing printed about gate shape: the same inspecting verify once the path is in the task's files; a verify that only hands a HEAD file to a runner (uv run pytest -q tests/x.py, bash tests/check.sh); a verify that reads a file which does not exist in HEAD (the durable-artifact case, a task creating what its gate reads); and git diff --name-only HEAD -- docs, where docs is a directory pathspec rather than a file being read.

The rule is computed from the verify string and git's HEAD, the same inputs gate_files_moved() uses — not from a list of known filenames — and it adds no per-gate or per-iteration cost: it runs once, in the plan phase, beside the two existing rules.

Scenario 33-gate-rewrite.sh plants a verify (grep -q ORIGINAL probe.txt with probe.txt unowned) that this rule now rejects at plan time. It is changed so it still exercises the runtime GATE REWRITE guard — for example by having the gate execute the committed file rather than grep it — and still asserts all three of its shapes; it is not deleted and its runtime assertions are not dropped.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/35-gate-unowned-file.sh plants the rejected case and at least the owned and executing accepted cases, and asserts exit codes and messages for each.

.claude/skills/loop-plan/SKILL.md gains a paragraph in the section that documents the gate-shape rules, stating rule 3 and its two escape hatches (put the file in files, or move the claim to acceptance), so a planner learns it rather than being rejected by it.

The new scenario file is added under .loop/tests/scenarios/ (run-all.sh globs that directory, so no registration edit is needed), and every document check-docs.sh holds to the suite size — README.md, .loop/README.md, .loop/manual.md, docs/briefs/B008-driver-in-python.md and this run's own brief — is updated in the same change so check-docs.sh stays green; check-docs.sh itself is not weakened, exempted or edited.

The whole offline suite (.loop/tests/run-all.sh) and uv run pytest -q stay green: existing scenarios keep asserting what they asserted before, and none is deleted or loosened to make room for this change.

tasks.title: Gate-shape lint rule 4: reject a gate that diffs against any ref other than HEAD
tasks.goal: Failure E in the brief: a scope guard written as git diff <plan-commit> became unpassable the moment any other task committed, and falsely reverted six finished tasks. A gate re-runs for the life of the plan, so any baseline fixed at plan time decays. This task adds a fourth rule to the same plan-time lint that T1 extended; git diff HEAD stays allowed because a work session cannot commit, so it still discriminates a session's edits from history. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.
acceptance: A plan is rejected (die, exit 1, before any iteration) when a task's verify runs git diff, git log or git rev-list against a named commit, tag, branch, relative ref or merge-base — including 4c911d7, HEAD~1, v1.0..HEAD, origin/main..HEAD and $(git merge-base HEAD main). A range that merely ends in HEAD is still a fixed baseline and is rejected.
The rejection line names the task id and then the ref it diffs against on the same line where the ref is a literal, and says the baseline decays on the next commit.
A verify that diffs against HEAD itself (git diff --name-only HEAD -- docs, git diff --quiet HEAD -- docs) is accepted with nothing printed about gate shape.
Rule 3 from T1 and the two original rules still behave exactly as before; this rule is added beside them in the same plan-phase lint and adds no per-iteration cost.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/36-gate-decaying-baseline.sh plants at least the named-commit rejection and the HEAD acceptance and asserts both.
.claude/skills/loop-plan/SKILL.md gains a paragraph in the gate-shape section stating rule 4 and why a HEAD diff is the one that stays sound.

tasks.title: Export the active task id and the gated task id to every gate in the sweep
tasks.goal: When a finished task's gate re-runs as a regression check, the only uncommitted work in the tree belongs to whichever task is being worked now, and a scope guard cannot tell that from a stray without knowing it. The consumer repo re-derived the active task by reimplementing the driver's selection rule; this task has the driver hand both ids to each gate instead. The names LOOP_ACTIVE_TASK (the task this iteration works) and LOOP_GATE_TASK (the task whose verify is running) are pinned by this plan because T4's advisory and this task's gate both depend on them. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.
acceptance: While the driver runs a task's verify, the verify's environment carries LOOP_ACTIVE_TASK set to the id of the task this iteration is working and LOOP_GATE_TASK set to the id of the task whose verify is running; they differ exactly when the gate is running as a regression check of another task.

Outside the gate sweep both variables are absent, not set to an empty string: work and review sessions do not see them, and a value inherited from the driver's own environment (as happens when the suite runs inside a gate) does not leak into any session.
The export adds no git invocation and no per-gate cost beyond setting two variables.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/37-gate-task-env.sh asserts both values in a regression-check gate and in the current task's own gate, and their absence in a session.

The two variables are documented where the loop documents verify commands for planners (.claude/skills/loop-plan/SKILL.md) and for operators (.loop/manual.md or .loop/README.md), including that a scope guard reading git diff HEAD should consult them.

tasks.title: Run a blocked task's own gate and report when it passes
tasks.goal: Two of the five stalled runs read blocked while their deliverables were complete and green; an operator had to run the gates by hand to see that the block was about something else. Today the current task is only added to the gate sweep when it claims done. This task adds it on blocked too and, when its gate passes, says so — as a signal, not a verdict: the status transition and the attempt charge do not change. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.

references.why: iterations.jsonl outcome is one of done, gate_fail, review_fail, blocked, and runstat recomputes every run-level signal from those records; this task adds signal, and a new outcome value or a changed record shape would make the driver and runstat silently disagree

acceptance: When the work session's outcome is blocked, the current task's own verify runs in that iteration's gate sweep alongside every done task's.

When that gate passes, the driver says so in three places, each naming the task and stating in words that its gate passes (the words gate and pass appear together): the iteration's warning line, the task's notes in .loop/state/state.json, and the run-end report printed after the final status banner. The session's own summary is still carried in the notes.
When that gate fails, nothing claims it passed, and it is not treated as a regression or a gate_fail: the iteration outcome stays blocked.

The status transition is unchanged: a blocked outcome still returns the task to pending with one attempt charged, the review session is still not run for it, and the iterations.jsonl record keeps outcome blocked — no new outcome value is introduced.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/39-blocked-gate-passes.sh asserts both the passing and the failing case.

tasks.title: Report the working tree when a work session leaves no proposal
tasks.goal: When a work session dies before writing its proposal, the driver records a fixed 'work session produced no proposal' with notes none, and then commits whatever the dead session left in the tree. In the consumer's arc that hid a finished deliverable for three consecutive iterations and stalled a run. This task makes the no-proposal path say whether the session changed the tree, and which paths, so the next reader can tell 'nothing happened' from 'work was done, died unreported, and has been committed'. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.

references.why: iterations.jsonl outcome is one of done, gate_fail, review_fail, blocked, and runstat recomputes every run-level signal from those records; this task adds signal, and a new outcome value or a changed record shape would make the driver and runstat silently disagree

When the session changed nothing, the notes say so in words that differ from the changed case and name no paths.
Paths the driver itself writes (telemetry, journal, state and plan under .loop/state/, transients under .loop/tmp/) are never reported as the session's work.

Status handling is unchanged: the outcome is still blocked with one attempt charged, the session's files are still committed by the driver's single iteration commit, and at most one git invocation is added to the iteration.

tasks.title: Name the task being worked on every GATE REGRESSION line
tasks.goal: GATE REGRESSION <id> is only ever printed for a task other than the one being worked, and when the cause is that task's own gate misreading the active task's work, the message names the only innocent party. It cost two operator interventions in one run. The driver already holds both ids; this task prints both. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.
acceptance: Every GATE REGRESSION warning keeps its existing leading form (GATE REGRESSION <reverted id>) and also names, on the same line, the task whose iteration the regression was detected in.
What reverts and what is charged is unchanged: the regressed task still returns to pending with one attempt charged, and its notes still point at its gate log.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/41-regression-names-both.sh asserts both ids on the line.

tasks.title: Halt on a second blocked iteration of a task whose inputs have not changed
tasks.goal: A memoryless session given identical inputs reaches an identical conclusion, so a second consecutive blocked on the same task with nothing changed in between cannot produce new information — it cost money and a stall halt that reported the second diagnosis, not the first. This task halts the run at that point and surfaces the first diagnosis. The discriminator is whether the session's inputs changed between the two attempts, which must ignore the driver's own per-iteration bookkeeping commit (telemetry, journal, state), since that changes every iteration. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh and runs .loop/tests/run-all.sh; neither is this task's to edit, and the driver restores either from HEAD if it is modified — put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file.

references.why: iterations.jsonl outcome is one of done, gate_fail, review_fail, blocked, and runstat recomputes every run-level signal from those records; this task adds signal, and a new outcome value or a changed record shape would make the driver and runstat silently disagree

acceptance: When an iteration ends blocked, the previous iteration worked the same task and also ended blocked, and nothing outside the driver's own bookkeeping under .loop/state/ changed in the repo between the start of those two sessions — in particular no path in the task's files — the run halts after that second iteration without starting a third session.
The halt message and the run-end report surface the first of the two blocked diagnoses (the earlier iteration's summary), not only the second, and name the task.

When the earlier blocked session did change something (for example a path in the task's files), the retry is allowed and the rule is re-evaluated on the following pair; a run in which the first blocked session edited a file and the next two did not halts after the third iteration, surfacing the second iteration's diagnosis.

The halt decides nothing about the task: its status stays as the normal blocked transition left it (pending, attempts charged as today); only the run stops, with a non-zero exit, and no iterations.jsonl outcome value is added.

Scenario 11-stall.sh still exercises the stall halt: if its two identical blocked iterations now trip this rule first, it is changed so its stub alters something between attempts and still asserts exit 3, run status stalled and 'no recorded progress'; it is not deleted.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/42-repeat-blocked-halts.sh asserts the unchanged and changed cases.

The new scenario file is added under .loop/tests/scenarios/ (run-all.sh globs that directory, so no registration edit is needed), and every document check-docs.sh holds to the suite size — README.md, .loop/README.md, .loop/manual.md, docs/briefs/B008-driver-in-python.md and this run's own brief — is updated in the same change so check-docs.sh stays green; check-docs.sh itself is not weakened, exempted or edited.

tasks.title: Refuse to plan, and fail check-brief, for a plannable brief whose journal already exists
tasks.goal: Nothing retires a brief, so a spent one reads plannable forever, and run.sh --plan-only against it overwrites .loop/state/state.json and re-derives work already on main. A run's journal is named for its plan, which is the brief's own name, so the existence of that journal is the test — no stamp, no new field. This task makes .loop/check-brief.sh report it and .loop/run.sh refuse to plan from it, with an explicit override so a deliberate re-plan after an aborted run stays possible. The override is pinned as a --replan flag because the gate has to invoke it. Retiring or stamping the brief is explicitly out of scope. The gate sources .loop/tests/lib.sh, which is not this task's to edit; the driver restores it from HEAD if it is modified, so put any helper the new scenario needs inside the scenario file. run-all.sh is in this task's files only for the check-brief step described below.
acceptance: .loop/check-brief.sh, given a brief that declares itself plannable and whose journal exists at .loop/state/journals/<brief filename without .md>.md, exits 1 and prints a problem line naming that journal path and saying the brief has already been run; a brief whose name ends .loop-brief.md is also matched by its journal without that suffix, since that is the number-and-slug run id a planner writes for it.
A plannable brief with no such journal, and a brief that does not declare itself plannable, are checked exactly as before (docs/briefs/0005-production-and-insights.md still exits 0).

.loop/run.sh, asked to plan from such a brief (including via --plan-only, and including when state.json holds a plan for a different brief), exits 1 before any session runs and before state.json or plan.md is deleted or rewritten; the message names the journal, says planning would overwrite .loop/state/state.json and re-derive work the brief already produced, and names the override.

.loop/run.sh --replan <brief> plans from such a brief anyway, and --replan is listed in run.sh --help; a brief never run plans normally without it. Resuming an existing plan for the same brief is not affected.

Nothing is marked, stamped, rewritten or retired: no brief's Status line or frontmatter is edited, including docs/briefs/0003-runstat-cli.md and docs/briefs/0004-runstat-review.md, which both declare ready to plan and both have journals.

run-all.sh stays green in this repo despite those two briefs (and this run's own brief, whose journal now exists): its check-brief step still checks every brief's structure, and the already-run finding is handled there explicitly rather than by exempting named briefs inside check-brief.sh or weakening its exit code when run directly.
A new scenario .loop/tests/scenarios/43-brief-already-run.sh asserts the refusal, the untouched state, the override and the never-run case.

The new scenario file is added under .loop/tests/scenarios/ (run-all.sh globs that directory, so no registration edit is needed), and every document check-docs.sh holds to the suite size — README.md, .loop/README.md, .loop/manual.md, docs/briefs/B008-driver-in-python.md and this run's own brief — is updated in the same change so check-docs.sh stays green; check-docs.sh itself is not weakened, exempted or edited.
